subject: Discovery recap: Resilience requirements & graceful degradation (Skyline Ops)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@skylineops.com>, Erin Park <erin.park@skylineops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: resilience goals & incident history (Skyline Ops)

Hi Jordan / Erin —

Thanks for taking the time earlier. Quick recap from our 45-minute discovery so we have alignment and concrete next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Production outages in Q4 and Q1 caused by a model-serving region failure and cache warm-up latency; several incidents lasted 15–45 minutes and impacted end-user search relevance.
- Current fallback is a CPU-hosted smaller model that increases latency and drops accuracy; users see inconsistent behavior during incidents.
- Limited visibility into per-request latency distribution and no automated rollbacks for bad model pushes.

Current stack as discussed:
- In-house front-end + SRE layer, model hosted in us-west-2 on managed GPU instances (mixed p3/p4).
- Prefix caching layer is custom, KV cache lives in same region, low cross-region replication.
- Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana; incident tracking in JIRA.

Success criteria you gave:
1) Max P95 gen latency during steady-state < 200ms for the primary path.
2) During region failure, failover to secondary region with service disruption < 60s (RTO target).
3) Graceful degradation: maintain a minimum utility (search recall) with a bounded quality delta (no more than 12% drop) when falling back to smaller models.
4) Clear audit logs and per-tenant SLO reporting for compliance.

Reliability considerations we talked about:
- Fallback model strategy: maintain a 'fallback family' of quantized models we can auto-route to when GPU capacity constrained.
- Cross-region replication for KV and prefix caches to hit the RTO target — we suggested warm standby in us-east-1.
- Automated policy-driven fallbacks: prioritize lower-latency, slightly lower-quality variants for critical endpoints and a conservative path for non-critical endpoints.

Proposed next steps (actions + owners/timing):
- I will send an incident timeline template and a short architecture checklist (attached) so you can annotate the last three outages — Dylan — EOD 3/16.
- Jordan / Erin: confirm the list of critical endpoints (top 10) you'd like us to treat as must-preserve for graceful degradation — requested by 3/18.
- Marissa & Aditya: schedule a 60-minute technical working session to walk through the fallback model plan and region failover options — target week of 3/23.
- I'll draft a preliminary SLA framing (incl. SLO definitions and penalties) for us to iterate on — Dylan — draft by 3/20.

Attachments included: skyline-incident-timeline.pdf (template), current-arch-diagram.png (from our notes), sla-draft-v1.docx (initial SLA outline).

Thanks again — I think there is a clear path to reducing outage blast radius while keeping cost predictable.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-03-15 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: resilience goals & incident history (Skyline Ops)

Dylan — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Incident details: the longer outage in January was actually a control-plane issue that caused an automated scale-down of GPUs in us-west-2; the warm-standby in us-east-1 exists but isn’t kept fully warmed (cost trade-offs). I will attach the January incident JIRA in a follow-up.
2) Critical endpoints: search-api (high priority), recommendations (high), alerts (medium), profile enrichment (low). We'll confirm the full top-10 list by 3/18 as requested.
3) SLA: we are open to an SLO banded approach (bronze/silver/gold) to map to different endpoints. Can you include a failure-mode appendix in the SLA draft?

One ask: can Redwood share an example playbook for an automated rollback triggered by latency/regression signals? We've seen noisy rollbacks in the past and want to understand guardrails.

I'll upload the January incident JIRA and our internal postmortem to the shared drive tonight.

—Jordan
Jordan Li
Head of Platform Engineering, Skyline Ops
jordan.li@skylineops.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jordan Li <jordan.li@skylineops.com>, Erin Park <erin.park@skylineops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-03-15 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: resilience goals & incident history (Skyline Ops)

Appreciate the quick replies and the added detail, Jordan. Yes — we'll include a failure-mode appendix in the SLA draft.

Regarding the automated rollback playbook: attaching a short example (in the attachments) and pasting a condensed flow here for quick reference: 
- Signal types: P50/P95/P99 latency spikes, token-error-rate increase, model quality regression from eval set.
- Triggering: threshold + sustained window + multi-signal confirmation.
- Pre-rollback checklist: notification to on-call, snapshot of KV/prefix cache, traffic mirroring to degraded path.
- Action: promote previous stable model or route to quantized fallback family; if cross-region failover is required, shift control-plane traffic to us-east-1 warm standby while keeping prefix cache read-only replication enabled.

We also recommend an incremental canary process (1%, 5%, 25%) with automated abort conditions to reduce noisy rollbacks.

Next internal step for Redwood: Marissa/Aditya, can you prepare a short proposal outlining cost delta for keeping a warm-standby vs. a cold standby with rapid warm-up? If you want, I can provide sample traffic curves from similar customers to help size.

Jordan/Erin: I'll send calendar invites for the working session (week of 3/23) and drop in preliminary SLO bands (bronze/silver/gold) for the endpoints you called out.

Thanks — I look forward to the artifacts you upload.

Best,
Dylan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jordan Li <jordan.li@skylineops.com>, Erin Park <erin.park@skylineops.com>
Date: 2026-03-16 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: resilience goals & incident history (Skyline Ops)

Looping in our cost ops and infra leads — putting a few bullets here so we have internal alignment before the working session: 

- Cost vs. availability: will prepare two options: (A) warm-standby (minimal replica kept warm in us-east-1, higher baseline cost) and (B) cold-standby with accelerated warm-up (lower baseline cost, longer RTO). Provide exact cost delta and expected RTO for both.
- Fallback model family: propose a 3-tier fallback family (full model => quantized medium => tiny CPU fallback). We'll show latency/quality tradeoffs per tier.
- Observability: propose per-endpoint SLO dashboards with per-route token-level latency breakdown + alerting based on regression on golden prompt set.

I'll draft these and attach to the working session invite. Dylan — can you confirm whether Skyline needs encrypted cross-region replication (they mentioned compliance concerns)? If yes, we will include KMS-based envelope encryption in the proposal.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
